text:
anya: Quick sync  propose a 'mini roles matrix' inside the invite drawer: 2-row compact grid with a tiny info chevron on each role that opens a bottom sheet on mobile or a small inline panel on desktop. Goal: reduce vertical scroll for frequent invites. Figma: https://figma.redwood/mini-matrix :link

Tom: Compact grid sounds promising. Question: how do we show permission summaries without making the grid unreadable? Suggest micro-teasers: role name + one-line summary, then the chevron reveals details.

Rui: Accessibility: each role tile must be a focusable element. Use `role=button` and `aria-expanded` when the detail panel is open. For bottom sheet: trap focus and add `aria-label="Role details for <role>"`. Announce expansion with `aria-live=polite`: "Viewer details opened".

Sarah: Copy idea for teaser: "Viewer — read access". Bottom sheet header: "Viewer role details". For SSO note in the detail area: show a concise warning badge: "SSO required to assign" with tooltip text: "This role can only be given to accounts linked to your IdP."

Kevin: Telemetry: add `invite.mini_matrix_open`, `invite.role_tile_expand`, `invite.bottomsheet_open`, `invite.sso_warning_seen`. Also record device breakpoint so we can compare mobile vs desktop behavior.

Tom: Mobile UX: bottom sheet should show a clear CTA "Assign role" and a secondary "Back". If user taps a role in the grid then navigates to Audit Logs, include `from=invite` in the URL so Audit can pre-fill role filter.

Rui: Keyboard navigation specifics: Arrow keys move between tiles, Enter/Space opens details. When sheet opens move focus to first interactive element inside. Provide `Esc` to close sheet and return focus to the originating tile. For inline panel on desktop, focus should go to the panel and the panel should be reachable after tabbing.

Anya: Regarding SSO enforcement toggle: product wants a two-step confirm when disabling enforcement. Draft copy: "Disabling SSO enforcement may allow users to sign in without your identity provider. To confirm, type your org name:". We should consider a gentler variant too.

Sarah: Legal prefers the stronger phrasing. If we need gentler, maybe: "Disabling SSO enforcement might allow sign-ins without your IdP." But legal usually wants "may". Also change primary CTA to "Confirm disable" for clarity.

Rui: Accessibility for the confirm: input must have `aria-label="Type organization name to confirm"` and the dialog should include an accessible error if the text doesn't match. Announce success/failure with `aria-live=assertive`.

Kevin: Add audit event `org.sso.enforcement_changed` and include `confirmed_by` and whether typed_confirm was used. Also log `affected_account_count` if we run the checklist step.

Tom: Small visual nit: the SSO warning badge should use icon+text (lock + "SSO") not color alone for colorblind accessibility. Ensure contrast passes AA.

Anya: For the bottom sheet details: include a small link "Who will be affected?" which opens a CSV download of affected accounts. That link needs an accessible name `Download affected accounts (CSV)`.

Rui: One more: when a role filter is applied in Audit via `from=invite`, show a dismissible banner: "Applied filter: Viewer (from Invite)" with a keyboard-focusable clear button. `Esc` should clear it when focused. Also update breadcrumb to include "Invites → Audit Logs" when navigated via that path.

Sarah: I'll finalize microcopy for the badges, confirmation modal, and bottom sheet CTAs and loop in legal.

Kevin: I'll add the telemetry tickets and include a metric for "time from drawer open to invite sent" so we can measure if mini matrix speeds things up.

Anya: Next steps: Tom to add mobile sheet + desktop inline mock (Figma), Rui to write keyboard/a11y checklist, Sarah to send copy to legal, Kevin to add telemetry. We'll run a 5-person mobile usability test next week. :sparkles:
